content_voiceover: This is the SELECT-D trial, another pivotal study in cancer associated thrombosis, this time comparing rivaroxaban against dalteparin over six months. Look at the two hazard ratios at the top. For VTE recurrence, the hazard ratio is zero point four three with a ninety five percent confidence interval of zero point one nine to zero point nine nine, so that crosses under one and is statistically significant, meaning rivaroxaban meaningfully reduced recurrent clot risk compared to dalteparin, which you can see reflected in the left graph where the yellow dalteparin curve climbs well above the blue dashed rivaroxaban curve after about month two. But for major bleeding, the hazard ratio flips the other direction, one point eight three, with a confidence interval of zero point six eight to four point nine six that crosses one, so it is not statistically significant, though the point estimate favors dalteparin and the right hand curve shows rivaroxaban trending higher for bleeding, especially in the first three months. So SELECT-D reinforces the same theme as Hokusai, DOACs can lower recurrent VTE but at a possible bleeding cost, and this trial in particular flagged an increased risk of GI and urologic tract bleeding with rivaroxaban.
keypoints: SELECT-D trial: rivaroxaban versus dalteparin, six month follow up
VTE recurrence significantly reduced with rivaroxaban: HR 0.43, CI 0.19 to 0.99
Major bleeding trended higher with rivaroxaban: HR 1.83, CI crosses 1, not significant
Rivaroxaban flagged increased GI and urologic tract bleeding
Confirms the DOAC tradeoff pattern seen in Hokusai VTE Cancer
keypoint_voiceover: SELECT-D showed rivaroxaban significantly cut recurrent VTE, hazard ratio zero point four three, but trended toward more major bleeding, hazard ratio one point eight three though not statistically significant, with particular concern for GI and urologic bleeding, echoing the pattern from Hokusai.
